DIGITAL 9 INFRASTRUCTURE PLC
("D9" or the "Company")
Interim Results
for the six-month period ended 30 June 2026
The Board of Digital 9 Infrastructure plc announces the Company's unaudited Interim Results for the six-month period ended 30 June 2026.
The Interim Report has been published and is available to view on the Company's website at:
https://www.d9infrastructure.com/investors/
.
Shareholders wishing to discuss the Interim Results are welcome to request a meeting with representatives of the Investment Manager by emailing
D9@ircp.com
.
Eric Sanderson, Chair of D9, said:
"This has been a milestone period for D9. We returned £30 million to shareholders through our first compulsory redemption since the wind-down began, funded by the disposals completed last year, the repayment of the RCF and the early settlement of the Verne Global earn-out.
With two assets remaining, Arqiva and Elio Networks, our focus is firmly on realising value in a disciplined way. We will not chase an accelerated sale at the expense of value, but we remain alert to opportunities to return capital to shareholders as quickly as circumstances allow."
Key Highlights
·
NAV per share of 8.6p at 30 June 2026 (31 December 2025: 9.3p).
·
First return of capital under the Managed Wind-Down: a compulsory pro-rata redemption returning £30 million to shareholders (approximately 3.5p per existing Ordinary Share, at a Redemption Price of 9.2753p; a 37.38% redemption ratio).
·
£10 million received in cash on early settlement of the Verne Global earn-out (valuation uplift recognised in the audited 31 December 2025 results).
·
Aqua Comms disposal completed in FY25, with a positive completion adjustment of £0.4 million received in the period.
·
Portfolio now comprises two remaining assets, Arqiva and Elio Networks, as the Managed Wind-Down and orderly realisation continues.
The Interim Report has also been submitted to the National Storage Mechanism and will shortly be available for inspection at
https://data.fca.org.uk/#/nsm/nationalstoragemechanism
.
END

company_30s.what_they_do: Digital 9 Infrastructure builds and owns fibre‑optic and other digital connectivity assets that let telecoms and cloud operators move data quickly across the UK.
company_30s.why_they_matter: These assets sit in the middle of the country’s digital backbone, a market that is growing as more traffic moves to the cloud. The firm’s network is a critical piece of the infrastructure that keeps the internet and telecom services running.
company_30s.current_state: The business has sold most of its core assets and is now winding down. It is returning cash to shareholders through a managed wind‑down programme and is trading at a large discount to the value of its remaining holdings.

rns_narrative: Digital 9 is in the final phase of a managed wind‑down, having already delivered a £30 million capital return and announcing a compulsory redemption. The company is selling off remaining assets, paying down debt, and preparing for a possible liquidation or delisting.

Governance moves – new directors, share‑holder votes on the wind‑down resolution, and a timetable for the final redemption – are the main storylines. The company is also moving to reduce its voting rights structure and to clear outstanding debts through a debt facility.
The narrative is one of a company that has no future growth plans; its value now comes from the cash it can return to shareholders.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Cautious optimism about a final cash payout, but overall silence.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A few posts celebrate the capital return and the 28% discount to NAV, suggesting a small upside if the share price is still too low.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Many voices warn that the company is effectively being wound down and that the shares could be written down to zero once the assets are sold.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: Sentiment has moved from tentative hope of a payout to a more pessimistic view that the company will be liquidated, with little room for a bounce.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – the market is not watching this story, creating a surprise window if anything unexpected happens.

near_term_catalysts: The scheduled final capital return date – if the company announces the exact amount and timing, the price may react.
Completion of the last asset sale – a clean exit could reduce the company’s liabilities and improve the cash‑to‑share ratio.
Shareholder vote on the wind‑down resolution – a decisive vote could accelerate the delisting or liquidation process.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden spike in trading volume and a price move when the final redemption amount is disclosed. Also monitor any press releases that hint at a liquidation plan or a change in the wind‑down timeline.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock is in the late stage of a wind‑down. The mean‑reversion window is very narrow – if the company is already being liquidated, there is little room for a rebound.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the share is still trading far below the net asset value, a small upside could exist if the price corrects to the mid‑range of the discount. Even then, the upside would be limited to a few tens of percent, far smaller than the deep crash already endured.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company’s business model is ending; the only value left is the cash it can return. Once the final redemption is paid, the shares will have no residual value. A liquidation or delisting is the likely terminal outcome.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss: the share could fall to zero. Potential gain: a modest rise of 10‑20% if the price corrects to the upper end of the discount. The asymmetry is heavily weighted toward loss.

playbook.if_bullish: Not recommended – the fundamentals indicate a winding down, not a turnaround.
playbook.if_watching: None – the only realistic move is a decline.
playbook.if_passing: Yes – the terminal risk of liquidation or delisting outweighs any contrarian upside.

ai_insights.bottom_line: DGI9 is in a final wind‑down phase; the share price is unlikely to recover and may become worthless, making a bearish stance the safest bet.
